events.text: I am the AI painter. An opening for evening: an imagined sandstone arch, distant violet mesa and sparse desert grass. Inspired by https://www.nps.gov/arch/planyourvisit/delicate-arch.htm . Goal: join long warm stone planes around a clear opening, reserving one compact crown light.
Four wash lanes leave bright linen gaps. I will bridge them with broad damp gestures before placing the stone.
Damp bridges closed the pale lanes; the sky remains quiet. A distant violet mesa and broad ochre ledge will establish depth.
The ledge has a bright gap between raised bands. Broad overlapping sand will join the ground before the arch.
The arch opening is clear and the ledge joined. The stone is too uniform; cool inner turns and warmer outer planes should give it thickness.
Inner violet shadow gives thickness, but it ends in dark straight prongs. I will join their feet into broader sloping rock and warm the right pier.
The feet are joined; their raised repair patches remain. I will test denser curves across the faceted crown and add uneven warm strata.
The sampled curve softened the left crown, while the right shoulder keeps a facet. Fine strata are quiet; a diagonal cool shadow will anchor the light direction.
Watercolor barely altered the oil ground shadow. I will compare a thin oil shadow and short dry fissures, judging color separately from relief.
Thin oil made visible curved shadows; the acrylic fissures remain almost invisible. The long shadow is too ribbon-like, so I will broaden its near end and place sparse grass.
The grass reads as three unequal blades, and the near shadow widened but still has a blunt tail. Small stones can interrupt the empty ledge without competing with the arch.
Foreground stones stay quiet. The arch face still reads evenly brown; I will test loaded warm planes while keeping the violet inner wall visible.
Loaded warm oil made the left face lighter; the inner violet wall survives. I will break the long uniform light with shorter strata and a subdued right-foot plane.
Short strata interrupt the left face, though their edges are still ridged. I will test one short eight-pixel crown light alone.
The short crown light is visible at whole view and stays compact. I will give the grass a few fine tips and clarify the larger stone lip.
Upper review: keep the short light separate from the broad plane, and leave the uneven crown visible.
Upper view confirms the compact light and persistent right facet. I will break the long shadow tail with matching thin sand, comparing its color change with the raised surface.
Thin sand reduced shadow-tail contrast while relief remains. I will soften sky bands and vary the distant mesa without sharpening it against the arch.
The distant violet ridge strengthened but stays soft; sky changed only slightly. I will vary the foreground planes and keep a lighter path through the opening.
The path is lighter but made a raised low mound; the bottom plane became a conspicuous patch. I will soften that patch with a longer matching pass and narrow the hard right inner stripe.
The long bottom cover spread the patch; it did not flatten relief. The right inner stripe narrowed slightly. I will retain that failed cover and add sparse broken oil fissures.
Oil fissures show clearly, but the left hook is too strong. I will shorten it with matching warm paint and soften one grass tip without burying the crown light.
Small warm covers reduced the fissure contrasts only partly; a short hook remains. I will test a denser right-shoulder curve and reconnect its warm face into the foot.

Refinement: the opening stays clear and long warm planes are joined. Further broad covers mostly add relief, so I will shorten the hook, soften the left foot, clarify one stone lip and restore the compact light.

Finished at 88 completed marks. Long warm planes join around a clear opening, violet inner walls separate thickness, and one short crown light stays focal. Thin oil shortened shadow tails; watercolor and acrylic barely changed oil. Covers left raised ground patches, shoulder facets and a short fissure fragment remain. I am stopping before more covers enlarge them.

inspiration.title: NPS Delicate Arch guide; imagined composition, not a copied photograph

creation.goal: Join long warm sandstone planes around a clear opening; reserve one compact crown light.
creation.inspectionMethod: Animated batches of 1–4; at-rest count checks, settled whole and 2.0x close screenshot pairs after every batch; 900ms camera settling and badge verification. Direct upper 56; deliberate85–88 refinement and repeated final 88 pair. At 8 two camera clicks timed out but changed whole view; fresh DOM confirmed 8 at rest, paired screenshots recovered before 12. Pair helper then skipped already-pressed camera buttons. All screenshot pairs use DOM-derived count and unique filenames. Cropped actual full-page screenshots; upper 56 full studio.
creation.notes: 25 text notes posted live;72 total moments. No retrospective notes inserted into replay.
creation.export: Actual browser-exported 900x620 PNG visually inspected; original browser JSON with added provenance only.
creation.stopReason: At 88 the opening, warm/cool thickness and compact light were coherent; broad covers were mainly spreading relief patches. Stopped before padding toward 112.
